texts.li: [their:friend] The first thing the traders of {FACTION} asked at the gate was whether {FRIEND_nameDef} still lives here. They've broken down on the road below with a full load, and among {FACTION}, this colony's name is one worth knocking on.\n\n{A_nameDef} could go down and help with the repair. If not, they'll buy {TALE} for {COUNT} silver and do the work themselves.

[tribal] A trading party of {FACTION} has stopped below the colony with a broken sledge. One of its runners split on a rock, and their pack animals can't drag it lopsided.\n\nThey'd be glad of {A_nameDef}'s hands, the best in the colony. Otherwise they'll pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE} and cut a new runner themselves.

[lowtech,!tribal] A merchant wagon of {FACTION} broke its axle on the track past the colony's fields. The merchants have unloaded half their goods into the mud, and one of them keeps saying it was a good axle, a very good axle.\n\n{A_nameDef} is the best hand in the colony for a job like this. Failing that, they'll pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE} and make a new axle themselves.

[!lowtech] A trade caravan of {FACTION} has pulled up on the road outside the colony. The hub of their cart's rear wheel cracked on the rocks further back, and they've come this far on a splint and a lot of rope.\n\nThey'd take {A_nameDef}'s help gladly. Or {COUNT} silver buys them {TALE} to patch it themselves.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to help
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gets under the load and comes back black to the elbows. The repair holds, and the merchants leave part of their goods behind as thanks.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} does what can be done, but the repair won't hold. The merchants thank {A_objective} anyway and limp on to look for better help.

li.label: Sell them the materials ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The merchants pay {COUNT} silver for {TALE}, fix what they can by the roadside and go on.

li.label: Wish them luck
li.outcome: The merchants lash the thing together with what they have, and creak on down the road.

texts.li: [their:grateful] {FACTION} would rather buy from friends, their rider says, and has brought an order to prove it: {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver, more than any trader would pay.\n\nIn five days they'll send for it, the whole order or none of it.

[their:grudge] {FACTION} have no love for the colony, and their rider makes that plain. But they are short, and no one else has what they need. They want {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver.\n\nThey'll send for it in five days, and they want all of it or none.

[lowtech] {FACTION} are running short, and their rider has come a long way to say so. They want {TALE} from the colony's stores, and will pay {COUNT} silver for it, well over a trader's price.\n\nIn five days they'll send people for it. Half an order is no use to them.

[!lowtech] An order has come in over the comms from {FACTION}. It was taken down word for word.

Wanted: {TALE}.
Price: {COUNT} silver, paid on collection.
Collection: in five days, the whole order or none of it.

It's well above a trader's price.

[winter] It has been a lean winter among {FACTION}. They ask whether the colony can sell them {TALE}, and offer {COUNT} silver, more than a trader would. Their people will come for it in five days, and they need all of it.

li.label: Take the order
li.outcome: {FACTION} have the colony's word. In five days they'll send for {TALE}.

li.label: Turn it down
li.outcome: No order is taken, and {FACTION} will look elsewhere.

reminder.li: {FACTION} will send for their order tomorrow: {TALE}.

coming.li: {FACTION} send for their order in {DAYS}: {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver.

done.li: [lowtech] {FACTION}'s people came for the order with a tally stick, counted out {TALE} twice over, and paid the {COUNT} silver in full.
[!lowtech] Every item was checked against their list. {FACTION}'s people came for the order, found {TALE} waiting, and paid the {COUNT} silver without haggling.

fail.li: [some] {FACTION}'s people came for {TALE}. The stores held {ITEM}, and they had been promised the whole order, so they took none of it. They won't be in a hurry to deal with the colony again.
[none] {FACTION}'s people came for {TALE} and found none of it in the stores. They went home with empty hands and a poorer opinion of the colony.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} won't be sending for their order after all.

texts.li: [their:grateful] {FACTION} speak well of this colony, so {X_nameDef}, a tinker of theirs, names a friend's price: {COUNT} silver, and every torn coat and nicked blade in the place will be sound by morning.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a tinker of {FACTION}, has pulled a handcart up to the colony, loaded with awls, whetstones, patches and pots of glue. For {COUNT} silver {X_nameDef} will go through everything the colony wears or fights with, and be gone in the morning.

[!lowtech] The grinder strapped to {X_nameDef}'s pack squeals when it turns, and {X_nameDef} gave it a turn at the gate to prove it works. {X_nameDef} is a mender from {FACTION}'s lands, and for {COUNT} silver will go through every worn coat and battered weapon in the colony before moving on.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} works through the pile, and every piece comes back mended: seams closed, straps replaced, edges ground true.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} packs up and heads for the next settlement.

li.label: Pay a little to have {X_objective} teach {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the evening showing {A_nameDef} how to close a seam, rivet a strap and true an edge, then left the pile of mending for {A_objective}.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} down with an awl and a pot of glue and went through the tinker's tricks one by one. The mending is {A_nameDef}'s job now.

texts.li: [their:grateful] A runner of {FACTION} came in at dawn with bad news. A fever is going through their settlement, and their healers are out of everything. They came to the colony first, the runner says, because {FACTION} remember who stood by them before. They ask for {TALE}, and can pay {COUNT} silver if they must.

[their:friend] {FACTION} have sent word, and asked for {FRIEND_nameDef} by name. A fever is going through their settlement and their medicine is gone. What they need is {TALE}, and they can pay {COUNT} silver for it if they must.

[lowtech] The runner from {FACTION} had learned the message by heart on the road, and said it at the gate in one breath.

"Fever in every house. The old ones and the babies worst. The healer has nothing left. Please."

{FACTION} need {TALE}, and can pay {COUNT} silver for it if they must.

[!lowtech] {FACTION} have sent an urgent message. There is fever in their settlement, and there has been no medicine for days. They ask the colony for {TALE}. If it must be bought, they can pay {COUNT} silver.
[winter] A winter cough has gone through {FACTION}'s settlement, and their medicine went with it. They'd like {TALE}, and offer {COUNT} silver, though they would clearly rather not part with it.

li.label: Send it as a gift
li.outcome: The {THING} goes out to the gate the same day, with no price asked. {FACTION} will have it by morning.

li.label: Sell it to them ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {FACTION} pay the {COUNT} silver for the {THING}. Their thanks are correct, and short.

li.label: We can't spare it
li.outcome: The colony keeps its medicine. {FACTION} will have to manage on their own.

li.label: Send half, with {A_nameDef}'s instructions
li.outcome: Half the {THING} goes to {FACTION} with a long letter from {A_nameDef}: who to treat first, how much to give, what to boil, and what not to bother with.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] Half the {THING} goes to {FACTION}, wrapped with a bundle of {A_nameDef}'s own notes on fevers, drawn as pictures for anyone who can't read. Their runner set off at a jog.
[past:healer] {A_nameDef} has fought fevers like this before, and sends half the {THING} with a page of advice. The first line says to boil all the water.

texts.li: [water] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} both claim the same spring, in the hills between their lands. The argument has gone on all season, and now both have asked the colony to judge. Each has sent someone to make its case at the colony's table, and each expects to win.

[herd] Sheep from {ENEMY}'s flocks strayed onto {FACTION}'s land last spring and lambed there. The ewes were theirs, say {ENEMY}, so the lambs are theirs. The grass was ours, say {FACTION}, and so is everything that grew fat on it.\n\nBoth have asked the colony to settle it.
[land] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} can't agree where one's land ends and the other's begins, along a strip of good bottomland both want to plant. They've asked the colony to draw the line.

[salvage,!lowtech] A cargo pod came down between the lands of {FACTION} and {ENEMY}, and both reached it the same morning. Each says it got there first. They've agreed to let the colony settle it, which mostly means each expects the colony to side with them.

li.label: Side with {FACTION}
li.outcome: The council finds for {FACTION}. They send their thanks, and {ENEMY} send nothing at all.

li.label: Side with {ENEMY}
li.outcome: The council finds for {ENEMY}, who are delighted. {FACTION} call the judgment bought, and say so to anyone who will listen.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} work it out
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} talks with both sides at length and gets them to a split that neither likes and both accept.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} looks for a middle way, but both sides walk out, each sure the colony favored the other.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: No judgment comes from the colony. {FACTION} and {ENEMY} will have to sort it out themselves.

texts.li: A week of warm nights and soft rain, and the crops in the open fields have shot up days ahead of themselves. {A_nameDef} has been out to look at them every morning, hands on hips.

[summer] Hot days, warm nights and a good soaking every few evenings: the crops in the colony's open fields have come on days ahead of time. {A_nameDef} says it's the best growing weather {A_pronoun} can remember.
[spring] Spring has come in mild and wet. In the open fields the young crops have taken to it, and they're days ahead of where they'd usually be.

[fall] A warm wind came up from the south overnight, and the cold has let go for a while. It should stay mild for several days: more growing days for the crops still in the ground, and fewer cold nights for the colony.
[spring] The icicles on the eaves have been dripping since morning. A warm spell has set in early, and should hold for several days, long enough to give the fields a head start.
Mild weather, out of season. It looks set to stay for several days.

[farming] {A_nameDef}'s spade struck bone at the edge of the field. Someone was buried there long before the colony came, with no marker left, and a few of their things went into the ground with them.
[mining] Cutting into the hillside, {A_nameDef} broke into a narrow hollow with a body in it, long dead and carefully laid out. Whoever buried them put their belongings in beside them.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} turned up old bones under a mound of stones, stained with red ochre and laid out with beads, a stone blade and a carved pipe. Someone was honored here once, long ago.
[!lowtech] Digging outside, {A_nameDef} found an old grave: a skeleton in the rags of a uniform, a rusted tag still on its neck chain, the name worn away. A bundle of belongings was buried beside it.
Working outside, {A_nameDef} turned up an old grave. There are bones, a few scraps of rotted cloth, and the things someone once thought the dead would need.

li.label: Rebury them properly
li.outcome: The bones go into fresh ground with their things beside them and a stone at the head. A few colonists stay by the grave for a while after.

li.label: Keep the grave goods
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} brings in what was buried, and the bones go back into the ground with nothing. More than one colonist says it was wrong, and says it to {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Leave it be
li.outcome: The grave is filled in and left as it was found.

texts.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} found a cedar box wedged in the roots of an old tree, its lid sealed with wax. Inside are letters tied in bundles, two people writing to each other over many years. The names and the town on them are from {FACTION}'s lands.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} pulled a dented tin box out of the rubble of an old building. Inside, wrapped in plastic, are years of letters between two people who lived a long way apart. The return address is a town in {FACTION}'s lands.

Working outside, {A_nameDef} turned up a sealed box of old letters between two people who were often apart. The top one begins: "The rain hasn't stopped since you left, and the roof has found three new places to leak."\n\nThe names on them are from {FACTION}'s lands.

li.label: Read them aloud at supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} reads them out after supper, one bundle after another. Most of it is about the price of things and whose child is sick, and the colony sits up for every word.

li.label: Send them on to {FACTION}
li.outcome: The letters go to {FACTION} unread, with the next traveler heading that way. Someone there may still know the names.

li.label: Put them away unread
li.outcome: The box goes on a shelf, still sealed.

titles.li: Two young people at the gate

texts.li: Two young people of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} and {TALE}, came to the colony after dark, out of breath and holding hands. Their families won't allow the match, so they ran. They ask to be taken in, and {A_nameDef} has already brought them bread and blankets.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} found two young people of {FACTION} hiding behind the woodpile at dawn, {X_nameDef} and {TALE}. Their families had promised each of them to someone else, so they ran off together. They ask to stay.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} and {TALE}, both of {FACTION}, walked in off the road with one bag between them. Their families have been feuding for years and won't hear of the two of them together, so they left.\n\n"We can work," {X_nameDef} said at the gate. "Anything," said {TALE}.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {TALE} are colonists now. Their families among {FACTION} are not pleased, and the two of them don't seem to mind.

li.label: Send them home
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks them back to the road home, and the two of them don't say a word the whole way. {FACTION} send their thanks.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {TALE} thank the colony for its time and set off again, looking for somewhere that will have them.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION} is here. {X_nameDef} came from {FACTION}'s lands with a few things from home, and will stay the day before heading back.

[lowtech] A traveler at the gate asked for {A_nameDef}. It's {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, who heard where {A_nameDef} had settled and walked all the way from {FACTION}'s lands to see it. {X_nameDef} brought a gift from home and will stay the day.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, {X_nameDef}, has turned up for a visit with a bag of things from home and a list of questions from the rest of the family. {X_nameDef} lives among {FACTION} now, and heads back tomorrow.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} thinks it over through supper and says yes. {A_nameDef} is already clearing a corner for {X_possessive} things.

li.label: Enjoy the visit
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spends the day with {A_nameDef}, and will head home with a full pack and messages for the family.

texts.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a fortune teller of {FACTION} with a deck of painted cards and a pouch of knucklebones, offers to read every colonist's fortune tonight for {COUNT} silver, and promises only the truth.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} reads palms and cards, and swears {X_pronoun} has never told a fortune that didn't come true, give or take the details. For {COUNT} silver, everyone in the colony can have theirs read tonight.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} reads fortunes until late, and every one of them is good.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shuffles the cards back into their box and moves on.

li.label: One reading, for {A_nameDef} only
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} read {A_nameDef}'s cards by candlelight and found good things in all of them. {A_nameDef} came out smiling and wouldn't say what.

outcomes.li: [!lowtech] {X_nameDef} read {A_nameDef}'s palm under the lamp and promised a long life and a short winter. {A_nameDef} has repeated it to everyone.

li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} turned over {A_nameDef}'s last card, looked at it for a long time, and put it away without a word. {A_nameDef} has been asking about it ever since.

lines.li: Someone far away thinks of you.
Your hands will make something that lasts.

outcomes.li: [unlucky] {X_nameDef} reads fortunes until late. Most of them are good, but {B_nameDef} was told to stay away from deep water and is taking it seriously.
[unlucky] Most of the fortunes {X_nameDef} reads are good ones. {B_nameDef}'s was not, and {B_nameDef} won't say what the cards showed.
[unlucky] The last card in {X_nameDef}'s deck went to {B_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} looked at it a moment too long, and {B_nameDef} has said very little since.
